title: Brainstorming has an inventor. Advertising executive Alex Osborn began developing it in 1939.
description:
Advertising executive Alex Osborn began developing it in 1939. He popularised the term in his 1953 book, Applied Imagination.

Go for quantity, withhold criticism, welcome wild ideas, combine and improve. He claimed groups would produce more ideas than people working alone.

Compared real groups of four with individuals working alone, whose ideas were pooled into pretend groups of four.

The pooled individuals significantly outperformed the real groups. Later research blamed production blocking: only one person can speak at a time.

Reviewed by Diehl and Stroebe in 1987. Groups brainstorming together produced fewer ideas than individuals working separately.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brainstorming (read): established that Alex Osborn, an American advertising executive, began developing the method in 1939, that the term was popularised in Applied Imagination (1953), his four rules (quantity, withhold criticism, welcome wild ideas, combine and improve), that Diehl and Stroebe in 1987 reviewed 22 studies and found groups brainstorming together produce fewer ideas than individuals working separately, and that production blocking (only one person can speak at a time) is a key cause.
- https://www.producttalk.org/2012/07/brainstorming-more-questions-than-answers (read): established that Taylor, Berry and Block published a 1958 study in Administrative Science Quarterly comparing groups of four with pooled individuals who never met, that the pooled individuals significantly outperformed the real groups, and that Osborn was an advertising executive without data for his claim that groups generate more ideas.
